provenance.prompt:
J.114 / Piper Quickstep — CELEBRATE action sprite sheet, attempt 1.

Create one clean game-art source sheet, exactly 1536 × 1536 pixels, true transparent RGBA, arranged as a precise 4-column × 3-row grid of twelve equal 384 × 512 px cells. Draw exactly TEN separate complete poses of the SAME Piper Quickstep, in row-major order, cells 0 through 9. Leave cells 10 and 11 fully empty and transparent. Every pose is a complete full-body figure, including every ponytail strand, fingertip, and both shoes. Keep each figure at one consistent scale and shared foot baseline. Maintain at least 60 pixels of fully transparent clearance between every figure part and all four edges of its cell. No overlap, touching, cropping, crossing, or bleed at any cell boundary. Clear empty gutters between every cell.

Use the supplied accepted Piper sheets only as references for her identity, anatomy, uniform, color palette, and rendering style. Do not copy their action poses. Piper is an adult human woman with warm-brown skin, athletic basketball-player proportions, expressive brown eyes, bright orange hair in a high ponytail tied behind her head, a russet-red sleeveless basketball jersey and shorts with cream/white piping and paired side stripes, and red-and-cream high-top basketball shoes with white socks. Preserve the same face, skin, hair, proportions, colors, and fully human anatomy in every pose: two arms, two hands with clear separated fingers, two legs and two shoes. Keep the uniform completely blank: no numbers, writing, marks, logos, jewelry, badges, or extra accessories.

All ten poses show one continuous, joyful, athletic post-score celebration, right-facing three-quarter profile, same camera angle and lighting. Make every pose visibly distinct, dynamically readable, and complete. Exact row-major sequence:
0. Grounded anticipation: knees flexed, shoulders relaxed, a restrained pleased smile as she recognizes the score.
1. Rise onto her toes; one hand begins a compact fist pump near shoulder level while the opposite arm bends naturally.
2. Small celebratory hop begins, torso lifted, both arms rising toward shoulder height.
3. Midair victory apex: full-body jump, both arms lifted in a wide celebratory V, hands/fingers distinct and clear of her hair.
4. Descend from the hop with arms still high but changing angles; ponytail follows the motion.
5. Land in a balanced athletic stance, elbows bent and both fists raised near her shoulders, smiling.
6. Turn her chest slightly more toward camera and punch one fist upward while the other arm stays bent by her ribs.
7. Extend one open hand outward in an inviting celebration gesture, other fist near her shoulder; keep both hands separated from her face and hair.
8. Step into balance and lower both arms in a distinct sweeping recovery motion.
9. FINISH at simulation tick 65: grounded confident victory stance, relaxed smile, one hand raised in a modest final salute, other hand on her hip, complete shoes visible.

The ten source-frame starts must correspond to the authoritative celebrate timing: ticks 0, 5, 10, 16, 24, 34, 44, 52, 59, and 65; frame 9 is the settled finish. Preserve strong separation between all poses and generous transparent margins. Prioritize readable full-body silhouettes over figure size.

The athlete sheet contains Piper only. Do NOT draw a ball, basketball, ball seams, hoop, rim, court, floor, ground shadow, glow, confetti, sparkles, smoke, scenery, background color, checkerboard, grid, dividers, border, text, numbers, logo, trophy, prop, UI, teammate, audience, or any other person. The basketball remains a separate runtime game object and must never be painted into the sprite. Preserve actual alpha transparency outside the character. Return only the sprite sheet.
